newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold demand steady despite price dip.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold demand steady despite price dip.

text.p: A fall in world bullion prices has so far failed to really spark gold demand in the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai, Dubai-based traders said on Sunday.
"It is normal demand, regular buying. Nothing spectacular because the (Indian) wedding demand is over," said a trader.
India's main marriage season ran from October to February and current demand was limited, traders said.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24-carat gold -- was quoted by local traders on Sunday at 4,835 UAE dirhams ($1,316.72), down from 5,025 dirhams on March 2.

Spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $349.10-60 an ounce. It has lost nearly four percent in value during the week because of weaker technicals and news that Switzerland planned to sell bullion to set up a fund for Holocaust victims.

"Turnover is lower than when prices hit $338...Buyers have no rush," said another trader, referring to gold's steep price decline in January and the first-half of February which prompted heavy buying and import demand in Dubai.
January saw a record 46.35 tonnes of the yellow metal imported into Dubai. February's data is expected next week.
Dubai wholesalers were largely taking a relaxed position but are expected to increase their buying closer to the official month-long Dubai Shopping Festival which starts on March 27.
"The gold souk is one of the main attractions for tourists coming for the festival...It is definitely going to be a big boost to companies in the souk," said one trader.
"Prices are too volatile at the moment ... we will buy when the festival starts," another said.

Festival organisers are hoping to attract tourists, particularly from the Indian subcontinent, the Gulf and Europe, to Dubai's gold and jewellery shops with offers of some of the world's cheapest retail gold and numerous prize raffles.
